sources.note: Full auto-caption transcript, read end to end.

sources.title: AI Engineer talk page: No Vibes Allowed (ai.engineer)
sources.note: Page with AI-generated article summary; carries timestamps and caveats on the 35k and 300k numbers. Summary text is third-party paraphrase.

sources.title: AI That Works #17 ACE / Claude Code context engineering with Vaibhav (transcript 42AzKZRNhsk)
sources.note: Full 2198-line transcript read in two chunks. Co-host Vaibhav Gupta; only Dex's arguments or those Dex endorses were carded.

sources.title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents (rosetta.to page with transcript)
sources.note: Page includes full transcript plus AI-generated Q&A summary.

sources.title: MLOps Community Agents in Production 2025: 12-factor Agents
sources.note: Page carries full transcript including Q&A with Skylar Payne; read fully.

sources.title: StartupHub.ai recap: AI's Codebase Conundrum
sources.note: Machine-drafted third-party recap of the No Vibes talk; no new Dex material beyond the talk. Contains one claim (ship a week's work in a day) not found in transcript.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: around the 40% line is where you're going to start to see some diminishing returns
cards.claim: Quality degrades once a context window is roughly 40% full (the 'dumb zone'), a variable guideline depending on task complexity.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as a guideline using Claude Code's ~168k usable tokens; 'your mileage may vary'; no data shown.
cards.landing: Phase routine: a context-budget checkpoint (wrap up and compact at ~40%) in the ship plan section 0 and CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: if you have too many MCPs in your coding agent, you are doing all your work in the dumb zone
cards.claim: Too many MCP tools consume the context budget so all work happens in the degraded zone.
cards.evidence_detail: Assertion, no numbers.
cards.landing: Audit enabled MCP servers and tool definitions for the phase sessions; keep tool surface minimal

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: intentional compaction
cards.claim: Instead of arguing on in a derailed session, have the agent compress the context into a reviewable markdown file and start a fresh session from it.
cards.evidence_detail: Team practice; no measurement.
cards.landing: Phase handoff artefact: the decisions journal / draft PR body as the compaction file that a new session onboards from (P1 cold-resume trial tests exactly this)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The exact files and line numbers that matter to the problem that we're solving.
cards.claim: A good compaction file names exact files and line numbers relevant to the task rather than narrative.
cards.evidence_detail: Shown as an example slide, no numbers.
cards.landing: Handoff template fields in the plan-@-sha draft PR body: file:line pointers, not prose

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the worst thing you can have is incorrect information, then missing information, and then just too much noise
cards.claim: Context should be optimised for correctness, completeness, size and trajectory, ranked by harm: wrong info worst, then missing info, then noise.
cards.evidence_detail: Framework stated without data.
cards.landing: Principle for the knowledge store: a stale or wrong stored diagnosis is worse than none; verify before store

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the next most likely token in this conversation is I better do something wrong
cards.claim: Repeatedly correcting or yelling at an agent builds a bad trajectory that biases it to keep failing, so restart instead of steering in place.
cards.evidence_detail: Mechanism explained informally; no experiment.
cards.landing: Routine rule: after two failed corrections, restart the phase from the journal rather than continuing

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Sub agents are not for anthropomorphizing roles. They are for controlling context.
cards.claim: Subagents exist to isolate expensive search/reading in a separate context and return a succinct finding, not to model job roles.
cards.evidence_detail: Design principle with illustrative example.
cards.landing: Custom agents under .claude/agents/: define by context-isolation job (locator, reader) not by role; extends the Haiku fixflow-explorer

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Frequent intentional compaction
cards.claim: Build the entire workflow (research, plan, implement) around context management, with compaction between phases to stay in the smart zone throughout.
cards.evidence_detail: Team practice credited with 2-3x throughput; no controlled measure.
cards.landing: Ship plan section 0 phase routine (one phase per new chat) is a version of this

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you're going to pull in the root context and then you pull in the subcontext
cards.claim: Progressive disclosure: root context file plus sub-context at each directory level so the agent loads only what its area needs.
cards.evidence_detail: Described as an option; he then argues it goes stale.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: split into root plus per-slice files or skills loaded on demand (slice folders exist per runtime)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the amount of lies you can find in any one part of your codebase
cards.claim: Documentation drifts: code is most truthful, then function names, comments, and docs hold the most 'lies'; persistent onboarding docs rot.
cards.evidence_detail: Joke chart (audience answer 'slop'), no data.
cards.landing: Knowledge store design: entries need freshness/verification-against-code; CLAUDE.md 'Keeping this file honest' section already addresses drift

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: We prefer is on demand compressed context.
cards.claim: Prefer generating a fresh research snapshot of the relevant code slice on demand (parallel subagents over vertical slices) over maintaining static onboarding docs: 'compressing truth'.
cards.evidence_detail: Preference stated; no comparison data.
cards.landing: A saved research workflow/skill that runs slice-wise explorers and writes a dated research doc; a candidate against growing CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Planning is about compression of intent.
cards.claim: A plan file is a compression of intent: exact steps, file names, code snippets and a test after every change, so even a weak model cannot go wrong.
cards.evidence_detail: Team practice; plans shown as slides.
cards.landing: Plan @ <sha> draft PR body template: include file names, snippets and per-step verification command

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: as your plans get longer, reliability goes up, readability goes down
cards.claim: Plan length trades reliability against human readability; each team must find its sweet spot.
cards.evidence_detail: Hand-drawn tradeoff curve; no data.
cards.landing: Budget for plan length in the phase routine; owner one-page view is the readable side of this tradeoff

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: how do we keep everybody on the team on the same page
cards.claim: The key purpose of code review is mental alignment; reviewing plans and research (not only diffs) keeps technical leaders aware as code volume grows.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument, credited to a Blake Smith article.
cards.landing: Owner review should target the plan and decisions journal first; one-page owner view already approximates this

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: putting his AMP threads on his pull requests
cards.claim: Attach the agent thread, prompts and build-passed evidence to the PR so reviewers see the journey, not just a wall of diff (credited to Mitchell Hashimoto).
cards.evidence_detail: Dex endorses a practice by another person; no data.
cards.landing: Link the session transcript or journal from the draft PR; evidence folder with sha256 manifest is an adjacent mechanism

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: a bad part of a plan is could be a hundred bad lines of code
cards.claim: Leverage hierarchy: bad research causes thousands of bad lines, a bad plan hundreds, a bad line one; spend human attention at the top of the pipeline.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule of thumb, no data.
cards.landing: Reviewer effort allocation: refuter on research/diagnosis and plan before implementation, not only on final diff

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Do not outsource the thinking.
cards.claim: AI can only amplify thinking already done; if you skip reading the plan the process does not work (tool spew of markdown files is a warning sign).
cards.evidence_detail: Parquet Java Hadoop-removal failure story: they threw out plans and went to a whiteboard.
cards.landing: Routine gate: a human-read checkpoint after plan; counter-signal against workflows that only generate artefacts nobody reads

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Specri development is broken. Not the idea, but the phrase.
cards.claim: 'Spec-driven development' is semantically diffused (a spec may mean a better prompt, a PRD, or library docs) and so no longer useful as a term.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument citing Fowler's semantic diffusion.
cards.landing: Nowhere obvious; naming hygiene for harness docs (define 'phase', 'plan', 'verifier' precisely)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If you don't onboard your agents, they will make stuff up.
cards.claim: Without onboarding context the agent invents; onboarding must be supplied either via repo docs or generated research.
cards.evidence_detail: Memento analogy.
cards.landing: P1 cold-resume trial measures precisely whether the repository alone onboards a fresh agent

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you don't always need a full research plan implement
cards.claim: Scale the process to the task: a button colour needs just a prompt, medium cross-repo work needs research then plan; ceiling rises with more compaction.
cards.evidence_detail: 2x2 sketch of task difficulty vs process weight.
cards.landing: Phase routine tiering: light path for small phases versus full path; effort routing by phase size

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Pick one tool and get some reps.
cards.claim: Do not min-max across Claude, Codex and other tools; calibrating how much context engineering a task needs takes repeated reps on one tool.
cards.evidence_detail: Advice.
cards.landing: Argues for running the routine repeatedly on one tool before judging it; relevant to the unrun phase routine

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: a team of three. It took eight weeks. It was really freaking hard
cards.claim: His team of three reached 2-3x throughput after an eight-week, difficult workflow rewrite that changed how they collaborate.
cards.evidence_detail: Self-reported 2-3x throughput, team of three, eight weeks; the ai.engineer page notes it is team-specific, not guaranteed.
cards.landing: Expectation setting: the phase routine may need weeks of iteration before it pays off

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we shipped 35,000 lines of code to BAML
cards.claim: Seven hours on a Saturday produced about 35,000 lines in BAML, partly codegen and golden files, which the BAML CEO estimated as 1-2 weeks of work; one PR merged a week later.
cards.evidence_detail: 35k lines / 7 hours / estimated 1-2 weeks; he notes some is codegen; the ai.engineer page says not controlled measurement.
cards.landing: Caution on line-count as a productivity measure; do not use as target for FixFlow phases

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I'm going to try to oneshot a fix to your 300,000line Rust codebase
cards.claim: He one-shot a fix to a 300,000-line Rust codebase (BAML) with research-plan-implement; the CTO merged it without realising it was a podcast bit.
cards.evidence_detail: 300k-line Rust codebase, Monday-night work, merged by Tuesday; compared plans with and without research and discarded bad research.
cards.landing: None directly; evidence that merged-PR acceptance is a proof used by him

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: staff engineers don't adopt AI because it doesn't make them that much faster
cards.claim: A growing rift: staff engineers skip AI, junior/mid use it and produce slop, seniors clean up; cultural change must come from the top.
cards.evidence_detail: Observation, no data.
cards.landing: Nowhere obvious (organisational, not harness config)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: There is no perfect prompt. There is no silver bullet.
cards.claim: The three phase names are not essential; the durable idea is compaction and staying in the smart zone, and 'harness engineering' is a subset of context engineering.
cards.evidence_detail: Assertion; early hint that RPI is provisional.
cards.landing: Treat the phase routine as revisable; decide by observed cold-resume results rather than naming

cards.source_title: AI Engineer talk page (No Vibes Allowed)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: documents matter only when they accurately compress relevant truth or intent
cards.claim: Markdown artefacts are only valuable if they accurately compress truth or intent and improve execution; accumulating documents for their own sake does not help.
cards.evidence_detail: Page's AI summary of the talk's argument (third-party paraphrase of Dex).
cards.landing: Test for knowledge-store entries: does it compress verified truth and change a later action

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Not every problem needs an agent.
cards.claim: A deterministic script would have done his Makefile-build agent task in 90 seconds; do not use an agent where known steps suffice.
cards.evidence_detail: Own story, two hours of prompt tuning vs a 90-second bash script.
cards.landing: Workflow library: put known fixed sequences in scripts/CI, reserve LLM steps for judgment

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: most production agents weren't that agentic at all. They were mostly just software
cards.claim: Production agents are mostly deterministic software with LLM steps inserted at the right places.
cards.evidence_detail: Based on conversations with 100+ founders/builders; no counts.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool scripts: deterministic skeleton (gates, CI) with model steps as nodes

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Own your control flow
cards.claim: Own the loop (prompt, switch on structured output, context builder, exit conditions) so you can break, summarise, judge and pause in code.
cards.evidence_detail: Design principle (factor 8).
cards.landing: Workflow scripts authored in code with explicit exit conditions; argues for saving them as reusable library

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you will always get like tighter, better, higher reliability results by controlling and limiting the number of tokens
cards.claim: Long context windows degrade reliability regardless of model size; keep the context small and focused.
cards.evidence_detail: Appeals to audience experience with 2M-token Gemini.
cards.landing: Supports one-phase-per-session; context budget policy

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: clear all the air pending errors out. Summarize them.
cards.claim: Own error handling in context: after a valid tool call, clear earlier errors and summarise rather than piling stack traces on the window.
cards.evidence_detail: Observed failure spin-outs; no numbers.
cards.landing: Backpressure scripts: trim failing test/build output to a short summary before it reaches the agent

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: if you're not looking at every single token
cards.claim: Own your prompts and context format; inspect every token and optimise density and clarity because the only lever on output is input.
cards.evidence_detail: Principle (factors 2-3).
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md and skill text reviewed for token density; supports trimming

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: small focused agents
cards.claim: Use micro-agents of roughly 3-10 steps inside a mostly deterministic pipeline (their deploy bot), handing back to code afterwards.
cards.evidence_detail: HumanLayer deploy bot; also stated 'less than 100 tools, less than 20 steps' in the MLOps version.
cards.landing: Custom agents and saved workflows as small bounded loops with deterministic gates

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: find something that is right at the boundary of what the model can do reliably
cards.claim: Value comes from engineering reliability at the frontier of what the model gets right only some of the time.
cards.evidence_detail: Notebook LM example.
cards.landing: Verifier effort should concentrate on failure modes the model sometimes gets wrong

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: agents should be stateless. You should own the state
cards.claim: Keep the agent as a stateless reducer; persist and own execution and business state outside it so runs can pause, resume and be launched from any trigger.
cards.evidence_detail: Factors 5, 6, 12.
cards.landing: State lives in the repo (journal, evidence folders), not in chat; supports cold resume

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Tool use is harmful.
cards.claim: Tool calls are just model-emitted JSON handled by deterministic code; treating tool use as magic obscures control.
cards.evidence_detail: Deliberately provocative framing (factor 4).
cards.landing: None direct

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: not here to bash frameworks. I would think of this as much as anything as a wish list
cards.claim: Frameworks should be treated as a feature wish-list; 12-factor is a set of requirements for them, not an anti-framework stance (4,000 stars in a month or two; 14 contributors).
cards.evidence_detail: Star and contributor counts as stated at the talk.
cards.landing: Nowhere obvious

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I think slashcompact is trash. I never use it.
cards.claim: Built-in /compact is generic and loses trajectory; do compaction manually into a file and start a fresh session ('clear' is the good primitive).
cards.evidence_detail: Personal practice; he says /compact is designed to be general and gets you to about 80%.
cards.landing: Hard rule for phase routine: no auto-compact reliance; write the handoff file and /clear

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we try to target like maximum 50% context
cards.claim: Target at most about 50% context utilisation per session (in the YC talk this tightens to under 40%).
cards.evidence_detail: Team target; he adds 'this doesn't always become true'. 50% in this episode, 40% in YC and Nov talks.
cards.landing: Context budget number for phases; shows his own figure moved from 50% to 40%

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Once a model looks for something and finds a bunch of irrelevant stuff that's in the context window forever
cards.claim: Irrelevant search results stay in context until compaction, so progress files should carry file paths and line numbers rather than letting the next agent search again.
cards.evidence_detail: Mechanism explanation.
cards.landing: Handoff format; also argues for locator agent (fixflow-explorer) returning paths only

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: they are for exactly one thing, which is context control
cards.claim: Subagents are mostly for read-only work; the parent should explicitly prompt 'use a sub agent' and tell it how to return; parallel subagents (e.g. one per test type) gave accuracy wins over one thread.
cards.evidence_detail: Go unit-test example; no numbers (Vaibhav echoes accuracy).
cards.landing: Agent file prompts that specify return format; use subagents for read-only research in phases

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: A bad line of research can lead you to a thousand bad lines of code.
cards.claim: Hierarchy of leverage including a fourth tier: the core prompt set that manages research and planning can cause 100,000 bad lines, so human attention goes upstream.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated hierarchy 1 / 10-100 / 1,000 / 100,000 bad lines.
cards.landing: Treat edits to CLAUDE.md, skills and agent files as the highest-risk change class needing verification (weeks of testing before change per YC talk)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: in our linear board we literally have like research in progress, research in review
cards.claim: Review states exist for every artefact stage on the ticket board (spec needed, research in review, plan in review, code review, ready for deploy), so humans review research and plan before code.
cards.evidence_detail: Linear column list shown.
cards.landing: Observable phase states (draft PR status labels) make routine compliance visible from outside, a cheap W2 answer short of hooks

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: What I read really closely in implementation is the tests.
cards.claim: When reviewing implementation, read the tests closely; passing well-designed tests gives confidence in code; code review is skipped on well-tested areas but applied where tests are thin or algorithmically nuanced.
cards.evidence_detail: Team policy; BAML merge queue merged the PR automatically when tests passed.
cards.landing: Reviewer weights tests (fail-before/pass-after) over diff; risk-tiered review by test coverage

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I only do TDD with agents.
cards.claim: Plans should make the first phase a failing test and then fix it, giving as many checkpoints as possible; the test commands must be trivial for the agent to run. (Stated by Vaibhav; Dex says he does the same and has a new plan prompt requiring failing test first.)
cards.evidence_detail: Credited mainly to the co-host in this passage; Dex endorses and describes his own prompt change.
cards.landing: Matches the reviewer's fail-before/pass-after requirement; plan template step 'write failing test first'

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can literally give it the shell command
cards.claim: Put exact verification shell commands after each file or step in the plan so the model runs them via its to-do list; 'automated verification' without a command is weak.
cards.evidence_detail: Shown with a build-process plan.
cards.landing: Plan template: each step carries the exact command and expected output

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Put it in your plan or better yet put it exactly directly in your prompt.
cards.claim: CLAUDE.md is injected with a note that it may not be relevant, so instructions that must be followed should go in the plan or the prompt, not CLAUDE.md.
cards.evidence_detail: He shows the injected reminder text in a captured trace of the request.
cards.landing: Move must-follow routine steps out of CLAUDE.md into the phase prompt / skill; supports the CLAUDE.md trim

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: A lot of what goes into the context window for claude is like system instructions.
cards.claim: Inspect the actual request body via a proxy (system prompt, built-in tools, CLAUDE.md, MCP tools) to know what the budget is spent on before the user's message.
cards.evidence_detail: Captured a real Claude call trace via a proxy and published it with the episode notes; no token counts spoken.
cards.landing: Measurement: capture a trace of a FixFlow session to see how many tokens CLAUDE.md and tool definitions use; the skipped measurement pipeline would deliver this

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the research was wrong a couple times. I had to like delete it, throw it out
cards.claim: Research output can be wrong (said the bug was already solved); read it, throw it out, add a failing test case to the spec, and restart; failed research can be compacted into a better prompt for the second attempt.
cards.evidence_detail: BAML assert bug live demo; first research said no bug.
cards.landing: Refuter on diagnoses; knowledge store entries must be verified and discardable

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can prompt to say like, hey, here's what we're not doing
cards.claim: Plans should state explicit non-goals to stop the implementer adding unrequested extras.
cards.evidence_detail: Observed in live plan review.
cards.landing: Plan @ sha template: 'not doing' section; reviewer checks diff against it

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The research one, You reject the PR and you would say do it this way.
cards.claim: Plan-with-research vs plan-without-research comparison: both reached the same core fix but only the researched plan followed the repo's test convention; skipping research is fine for small issues but loses repo conventions.
cards.evidence_detail: One-bug comparison; research plan shorter; two PRs, one closed.
cards.landing: Rule of thumb for skipping research on small phases

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If you tell Claude to think deeply you get the thinking tokens. This can backfire.
cards.claim: More thinking is not always better; ultrathink can make the model over-attend to earlier instructions and ignore later corrections.
cards.evidence_detail: Personal experience, no data.
cards.landing: Early precedent for the medium-beats-xhigh finding; supports effort routing for verifiers

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Even the prompts we write for Opus, we don't use them for Sonnet
cards.claim: Prompts tuned for one model do not transfer; Opus prompts are not reused for Sonnet or o3 because attention differs.
cards.evidence_detail: Team experience.
cards.landing: Agent/skill files for Haiku or Sonnet workers need their own tuning separate from Opus phase prompts

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: consider just making a script that does it exactly how you want it.
cards.claim: Replace noisy MCP tool output with a script that returns context-optimised markdown (e.g. a Linear ticket with description and comments in one call).
cards.evidence_detail: HumanLayer ticket-pulling tool; MCP JSON described as very noisy.
cards.landing: Backpressure and fetch wrappers: run_silent-style scripts for gh/CI/Alembic output

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Open cloud code in the integrated terminal
cards.claim: Run the agent in the IDE terminal with the extension so it receives LSP/type errors; enable Python type checking and select the right interpreter so feedback exists.
cards.evidence_detail: Practical tip; no numbers.
cards.landing: Mypy strict/Ruff/tsc as automatic feedback; ensure agent sessions can see typecheck errors

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: it's guaranteed that the more files in a certain directory the worse it's going to be
cards.claim: Codebase shape affects agents: identical file names (page.tsx) and inconsistent package scripts or naming make search harder; one team member spent over two weeks moving to Turbo so agents run uniform top-level commands.
cards.evidence_detail: Two weeks of repo restructuring; Vaibhav also stresses consistent nomenclature.
cards.landing: Single canonical command set (npm run, pytest, alembic) documented once; naming consistency checks

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can add additional directories and then claude will be able to work
cards.claim: Multi-repo work can be handled by granting additional directories in settings.json; symlinks may be skipped by search tools so hard links work better.
cards.evidence_detail: Team practice for BAML plus cloud repo.
cards.landing: Nowhere obvious (single monorepo)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I shipped six PRs last Thursday and I haven't opened a nonmarkdown file
cards.claim: He shipped six PRs in a day and had not opened a non-markdown file in an editor in over a month (almost two months by the YC talk).
cards.evidence_detail: Self-report; also an engineer shipping 2,000 lines of Go per day that he could not review.
cards.landing: None; motivates plan-level review

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: everyone try cloud code for the first 10 minutes of a task
cards.claim: Adoption heuristic: try the agent for 10 minutes; if no happy path within 30 minutes, fall back; and restart attempts quickly (the shoot-again-immediately analogy). (The 10-minute rule is stated by Vaibhav, Dex adds the restart tweak.)
cards.evidence_detail: Time-boxed rule of thumb.
cards.landing: Timebox in phase routine: abandon and restart a phase session after fixed attempts

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the research prompt. It's 300 lines of markdown.
cards.claim: The research slash command is a 300-line prompt with subagent instructions and was tuned by a team member; slash commands are tested for weeks before anyone may change them.
cards.evidence_detail: 300-line research prompt; 'test those for weeks' appears in the YC talk.
cards.landing: Skills treated as tested artefacts with change control; counterweight to the CLAUDE.md length concern for command prompts

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: don't forget to read everything the model outputs
cards.claim: Closing takeaway: manage context via subagents and frequent compaction, steer, and read all output because research is the highest leverage and if wrong nothing else works.
cards.evidence_detail: Summary of the episode.
cards.landing: Human-read research/plan gates in routine

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: our goal all the time is to keep context utilization under 40%
cards.claim: In the implement phase update the plan file with done status after each phase and move to a new context window.
cards.evidence_detail: Team practice; 40% target.
cards.landing: Plan file doubles as progress tracker; each phase starts in a new session (matches harness)

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If I'm shouting at Claude, it's because the plan was bad.
cards.claim: If the plan is good the implementer needs no correction; frustration in implementation signals a plan defect, not an implementation one.
cards.evidence_detail: Experience.
cards.landing: Failure triage rule: when a phase goes wrong, return to the plan and record it in the journal

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I can sure as heck read 200 lines of an implementation plan.
cards.claim: Review a ~200-line plan instead of a 2,000-line PR to keep mental alignment (a teammate had delivered 20,000-line Go PRs he could not review).
cards.evidence_detail: 200 vs 2,000-line comparison; 20,000-line PR every couple of days.
cards.landing: Owner one-page view and PR plan section as the primary review object

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: our cloud MD and our slash commands are like we basically like test those for weeks
cards.claim: CLAUDE.md and slash commands are tested for weeks before anyone is allowed to change them because they are the highest-leverage lines.
cards.evidence_detail: Team policy statement.
cards.landing: Gate on CLAUDE.md trim and skills: test before merge, consistent with the knowledge-store pilot gating

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: This is a team of three in a month. These are credits
cards.claim: Heavy token spend was judged worth it for the time saved (three-person team, one month, on API credits rather than a max plan); goal list includes 'spend as many tokens as possible'.
cards.evidence_detail: No figure stated.
cards.landing: Cost context for effort routing; cheap-but-correct trade-off

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: he's getting a shout out anyways
cards.claim: Ralph Wiggum loop (same prompt looped overnight) is endorsed as a smart use of coding agents if you understand context windows; he links Geoff Huntley's article.
cards.evidence_detail: 12-hour overnight loop on a live stream, per Huntley; Dex's remark that Huntley is being humble.
cards.landing: Loop-style fresh-context-per-iteration as a pattern for mechanical tasks (later he limits this; see other readers)

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The challenge of like playing telephone
cards.claim: Subagent hand-back is lossy 'telephone': how the parent prompts the child to return findings determines quality, so prompt the return format.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as an open challenge.
cards.landing: fixflow-explorer agent file: specify output contract (paths, line numbers, confidence)

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: ingested data from 100,000 developers
cards.claim: Cites the Stanford study of 100,000 developers: AI use creates rework and can be counterproductive on complex brownfield work.
cards.evidence_detail: Third-party study (Stanford, 100,000 developers) cited by Dex; he does not give figures here.
cards.landing: Context for why brownfield FixFlow needs guardrails

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I still read all the tests, but I no longer read every line of code
cards.claim: After switching to spec-first he reads tests and specs but not every code line; trust is placed in reviewed specs plus tests.
cards.evidence_detail: Personal practice; later retractions are covered by other readers.
cards.landing: Reviewer protocol reads tests first; owner view; note this was later revised so treat as a baseline claim

cards.source_title: YC Root Access: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the idea of sitting and talking to an agent for two hours
cards.claim: Endorses Sean Grove's 'specs are the new code' view as an important idea (spec as source, not prompts thrown away), and names it a favourite AIE talk.
cards.evidence_detail: Guest idea Dex endorses; in Nov 2025 he backs away from the phrase 'spec-driven development'.
cards.landing: Nowhere obvious

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Can you imagine if your REST API failed on 20% of requests?
cards.claim: With AI, accuracy joins latency, uptime, cost and security as a performance dimension; an 80% agent is not production-ready, and context engineering is about reliability.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument, framing 80% quality as an outage.
cards.landing: Acceptance bar for harness claims: measured reliability, not a plausible-looking run

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: This is more meaning dense. The LLM has to read less stuff
cards.claim: Use XML-like traces in a single user message rather than verbose JSON/tool-message lists, for token efficiency and meaning density.
cards.evidence_detail: Claimed benefit, no measurement.
cards.landing: Format of handoff/journal and CLAUDE.md content: dense, tagged blocks

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: before the output comes out, we're going to use a really small dumb model
cards.claim: Insert a small, dumb model as a guardrail on tool output when you own the loop; safety comes from controlling every token in and out.
cards.evidence_detail: Answer to a safety Q&A; no data.
cards.landing: Cheap-model verifier/guardrail steps inside workflows (cost-routed verification)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can make assertions about the intent of the output
cards.claim: Evals as deterministic assertions on the structured next-step intent of an agent trace, given a trace as input (BAML tests).
cards.evidence_detail: Open-source Linear agent example with ~10 tools incl. 3 ways to contact a human.
cards.landing: Assertable traces: have the phase routine emit a structured trace so compliance can be asserted rather than self-reported (soft alternative to hooks)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: There's no magic abstraction that solves the memory problem.
cards.claim: There is no off-the-shelf memory abstraction; teams with good long-term agent memory built it from scratch for the use case.
cards.evidence_detail: Example of AI math tutors with weeks/months of memory.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store pilot: custom, task-specific store rather than a generic memory product

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Small focus agents, less than 100 tools, less than 20 steps.
cards.claim: Keep agents small: under ~100 tools and under ~20 steps gives reliable results.
cards.evidence_detail: Numeric rule of thumb, no data (AIEWF version says 3-10 step loops).
cards.landing: Cap on tool count and steps per custom agent or workflow node

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: one of the big takeaways there
cards.claim: Constrained JSON generation hurts code quality (escaped newlines are poorly tokenised); let the model write code in its natural form.
cards.evidence_detail: Mechanistic logit/tokenizer argument in Q&A.
cards.landing: Nowhere obvious

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Put it in your slack, put it in your email. Your adoption will go up.
cards.claim: Meet users in their existing channels (Slack, email) and design for asynchronous human contact by agents with stateful control flow.
cards.evidence_detail: Observation from builders.
cards.landing: Owner comms: draft PR and email-style closing message rather than a new dashboard; nowhere beyond that

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: As they get smarter, there will always be a thing they're not good at.
cards.claim: As models improve, the frontier of failure moves but never vanishes, so engineering principles keep paying off.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument.
cards.landing: Justifies keeping verifiers even as models improve

cards.source_title: StartupHub.ai recap of No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: other
cards.quote: ship a week's worth of work in a single day
cards.claim: A machine-drafted recap restates the talk's claims (300k-line Rust, a week's work in a day) and says implementation must adhere to the plan under 40% context; the 'week in a day' phrase is the recap's gloss of the 35k/7-hour story.
cards.evidence_detail: Third-party summary; no new data; framing exaggerates (he said 1-2 weeks estimated in 7 hours, partly codegen).
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (use primary talk, not recap)

No slides read; code/prompt examples shown in talks (research/plan prompts, plan snippets) were not visible in transcripts, so their content is not carded.
The StartupHub recap carries one claim ('a week's worth of work in a single day') not present in the primary transcript; carded as marketing/other.
